name: Internet Token LiquidityUnifier unvalidated V3 pool callback mint
summary: LiquidityUnifier.swapV3(token, pool) is permissionless and accepts any contract whose token0()/token1() return the reward token and the caller-chosen token; it never checks a Uniswap factory or registry. It stores the caller-supplied pool in currentPoolV3 and calls its swap(), and uniswapV3SwapCallback then mints INT to currentPoolV3 in an amount the caller controls, guarded only by msg.sender == currentPoolV3. The validateSupply modifier is defeated inside the same call by burning the minted INT through the Convertor and re-minting it after swapV3 returns. Any caller can therefore mint unbacked INT through the TOKEN_MINTER role the unifier holds and sell it into protocol-owned liquidity, breaking the invariant that INT is minted only against a genuine pool swap of the configured swapAmount.
notes: The IntV3Initializer 0xc1494cb284c8d794497468c560ae301864e5bd26, executed by Safe 0x0c02d2d320c62d4088840a459fe8862c802fba78, granted LiquidityUnifier the TOKEN_MINTER role in RoleStore 0xd5d1a16084a116f8a6c2c706c110dbad2e99be83 (roleCache[unifier][TOKEN_MINTER] 0 -> 1). Without it the callback's RewardToken.mint reverts, so the role is necessary to the exploited condition; the unifier was deployed 23,272 blocks earlier without it and no later grant, revoke or unifier configuration call preceded the exploit.

Component 1 is the first exercise's depletion of the protocol-owned INT/WETH Uniswap V3 pool 0xdec6eadbd8ed3f655cba4bb4eeff6fb43b16969d. Components 2 and 3 are five later copycat transactions by other actors repeating the same swapV3 fake-pool mint before the TOKEN_MINTER role was revoked; they took WETH from the same pool and USDC from two Uniswap V4 USDC/INT pools. Unbacked INT kept by attackers (764,145,702.183763063166443405 INT by the first attacker, later burned) is dilution, not measured victim depletion. Copycat WETH is valued at the first-exercise quote; all merged transactions fall within 2,744 seconds.
